- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is high (e.g., >0.7) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is low or negative (e.g., <0.3) — model misses downward momentum or fails to adjust for bearish signals.
- Lag in response to sentiment shifts: model often reacts 1–2 days after sentiment changes, especially when sentiment turns bullish or bearish sharply.
- Mean reversion bias: model overweights recent highs/lows, failing to revert to historical mean unless sentiment strongly supports the trend.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts are prone to overconfidence in short-term momentum; sentiment should be weighted more heavily for medium-term (10–30d) forecasts.
- When sentiment is volatile (rapid swings), model tends to smooth out extremes — underestimates sharp reversals or overestimates consolidation periods.
